reviews.comment: Great lectures, very available to students. Learned all our names and answered questions helpfully. Thermo is hard, but he and the textbook help it make more sense. He even let us persuade him to give extra credit. Exams are difficult but fair. Dr. Antao is one of the best and nicest professors I have had by far!

He is very kind and knows plasma. But, his teaching style is abysmal, there was a lack of homeworks to learn from, and exams and project were graded way too hard. He handwrites complex charts that can EASILY be googled the lack of prepared slides really wastes class time. The course is stacked but undergrads are given the same assignments as grads.

Read the textbook when concepts confuse you and go to office hours for clarifications. Dr. Antao is easily one of the most kind and caring professors I have had at Texas A&M, he took the time to know everyone by name and was always patient when I asked stupid questions. The exams are tough, but an A is attainable with some elbow grease.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A professor who truly cares about his students. He gives a quiz at the end of the week which is no surprise and honestly, it was a great way to keep us engaged throughout the week. Common exams so I can't really rate him there. The practice he gives for the exam is pretty generic (textbook examples). Overall one of the better options for thermo.

He evidently cares to know his students (by name) and help us learn the concepts. He teaches in a clear and organized way and frequently engages the class in critical thinking. He's incredibly receptive to questions and is very helpful in office hours. HWs are doable and exams are doable, we do a lot of practice problems in class.

He teaches in a way that is very good for learning, just not always to get the best grade. He makes students engage in critical thinking and his tests are harder than some other profs but not like outrageously hard.

I wasn't a huge fan of Dr. Antao's teaching style. There are other professors that teach the material much better. Dr. Antao kinda over-explains everything and sometimes makes it harder than it has to be. He's a nice guy and wants you to succeed. If you read the textbook and come to class prepared then it's really not that bad of a class.

Great thermo prof! Homeworks don't take long, and are helpful in preparing for exams. Quizzes are mostly conceptual or basic calculations. You will need to read the book to grasp the material (lectures are helpful, but this is the nature of thermo). Was very helpful answering questions in office hours. Makes an effort to get to know his students.

Dr. Antao was a very great prof to have for MEEN 315. He makes a point of getting on a first name basis with all of his students and is very good at teaching the material. He wants to see you succeed but you have to put in the effort. Thermo is just hard but he makes it doable. Totally recommend his class.

Prof Antao is caring and understandable to all students. He goes out of his way to get to know you as a student. While he does this, his lectures are sometimes hard to follow and the tests he gives are probably the hardest out of all MEEN 315 professors. If you do not read the textbook, you will fall behind very fast!

Dr. Antao definitely cares about his students and wants them to learn the material well and think through their process, which is really important for thermo. He doesn't believe in just handing out answers, which I respect.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Antao was a great professor but was very stern and doesn't like dumb questions. His grade distribution isn't great but if you pay attention and study, an A is very achievable.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Antao was a pretty good professor for Thermodynamics. He explained topics pretty well during lecture, although sometimes he did get mixed up about things. Homework does take up a good amount of time, and tests can be difficult. However, participation in class can earn extra credit, which is nice. Reading the book is definitely recommended.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He makes you work hard for your grade. He is available for office hours, but that may not always be the most helpful. He tries to make this class a graduate level course. Tests are important, and he expects alot out of you.

Good professor as far as getting you to focus in class, does his best to make tough content easy to understand. His exams are unfairly long, requires you to come almost an hour beforehand to start test and was way too long, however does give almost a 5% curve on your final semester grades if you participate. Easy to get an A if you maximize that.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Emphasizes going to office hours, but will only tell you (once there) to "read the book" or to "just do the math." Admitted to not planning lectures (obvious). Final was 95% unit conversion (fkn hard) & 5% actual fluids (easy). Taught things wrong & didn't understand his own work. Comes off as nice but is actually a tool. Exams were crazy long.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Save yourself from a terrible Fluids class and take another professor. He seems like he cares, but that facade quickly fades when you get exams back. His exams are WAY too long. He changes grading criteria throughout the semester and admits to not preparing lecture notes and in office hours he just tells you to read the book. Barely scraped an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS
